+# --- KF-048: the per-run HOME carries a codex auth.json with a placeholder refresh token (Sprint 261) ---
+# snap_docker: a docker wrapper that, on the first `docker run`, copies the mounted HOME's
+# .codex/ to $T/snap (mode preserved) before handing over to the stub; the HOME itself is
+# deleted at exit.
+snap_docker() {
+  mv "$T/docker" "$T/docker.inner"
+  cat > "$T/docker" <<EOF
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+if [[ "\${1:-}" == run && ! -e "$T/snap" ]]; then
+  prev=""
+  for a in "\$@"; do
+    if [[ "\$prev" == -v && "\$a" == *:/home/evaluser* ]]; then mkdir -p "$T/snap"; cp -a "\${a%%:*}/.codex" "$T/snap/"; fi
+    prev="\$a"
+  done
+fi
+exec "$T/docker.inner" "\$@"
+EOF
+  chmod +x "$T/docker"
+}
+
+@test "container: KF-048 — the per-run auth.json carries the placeholder refresh token (never the host's), keeps every other key, mode 0600; the host file is untouched" {
+  cat > "$T/home/.codex/auth.json" <<'JSON'
+{"OPENAI_API_KEY": null, "auth_mode": "chatgpt", "last_refresh": "2026-10-18T00:00:00Z", "extra": {"k": 1},
+ "tokens": {"access_token": "x.y.z", "refresh_token": "R", "id_token": "i.d.t", "account_id": "acct-1"}}
+JSON
+  local before; before="$(python3 -I -c 'import hashlib,sys; print(hashlib.sha256(open(sys.argv[1],"rb").read()).hexdigest())' "$T/home/.codex/auth.json")"
+  snap_docker
+  run "$PR" --task-yaml "$BUILD" --arm a1_full --run-dir "$T/run" --run-id r1 --trial 1 --source-tree "$T/src" \
+    --suite-file "$T/suite.yaml" --executor container --docker-bin "$T/docker"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  local c="$T/snap/.codex/auth.json"
+  [ -f "$c" ]
+  [ "$(stat -c %a "$c")" = 600 ]
+  jq -e '.tokens.refresh_token == "loa-ablation-no-refresh-token"
+         and .tokens.access_token == "x.y.z" and .tokens.id_token == "i.d.t" and .tokens.account_id == "acct-1"
+         and has("OPENAI_API_KEY") and .auth_mode == "chatgpt" and .last_refresh == "2026-10-18T00:00:00Z"
+         and .extra.k == 1' "$c"
+  ! grep -q '"R"' "$c"
+  [ "$(cat "$T/snap/.codex/config.toml")" = "model = 'x'" ]
+  # the host file is byte-identical and still carries its refresh token
+  [ "$(python3 -I -c 'import hashlib,sys; print(hashlib.sha256(open(sys.argv[1],"rb").read()).hexdigest())' "$T/home/.codex/auth.json")" = "$before" ]
+  jq -e '.tokens.refresh_token == "R"' "$T/home/.codex/auth.json"
+  # no token value reaches the docker argv
+  ! tr '\0' '\n' < "$T/dlog/run-1.argv" | grep -qE 'x\.y\.z|i\.d\.t'
+}
+
+@test "container: KF-048 — an unreadable auth.json gives the run no codex credential, one WARN line, and the run proceeds" {
+  printf 'not json {\n' > "$T/home/.codex/auth.json"
+  snap_docker
+  run "$PR" --task-yaml "$BUILD" --arm a1_full --run-dir "$T/run" --run-id r1 --trial 1 --source-tree "$T/src" \
+    --suite-file "$T/suite.yaml" --executor container --docker-bin "$T/docker"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  [ "$(grep -c 'pipeline-run: WARN codex auth.json unreadable; the run has no codex credential' <<<"$output")" -eq 1 ]
+  [ ! -e "$T/snap/.codex/auth.json" ]
+  [ -f "$T/snap/.codex/config.toml" ]
+  ! grep -q 'codex/auth.json' "$T/dlog/run-1.mounts"
+}
+
+@test "container: KF-048 — a JSON auth.json that is not an object is unreadable too" {
+  printf '[1, 2]\n' > "$T/home/.codex/auth.json"
+  snap_docker
+  run "$PR" --task-yaml "$BUILD" --arm a1_full --run-dir "$T/run" --run-id r1 --trial 1 --source-tree "$T/src" \
+    --suite-file "$T/suite.yaml" --executor container --docker-bin "$T/docker"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  grep -q 'pipeline-run: WARN codex auth.json unreadable' <<<"$output"
+  [ ! -e "$T/snap/.codex/auth.json" ]
+}

# --- KF-048: the codex access-token freshness pre-flight (Sprint 261) ------------------------
# codex_auth <exp offset s> — a crafted auth.json whose access token is h.<base64url({"exp": now+offset})>.s;
# prints the exp instant (ISO 8601 UTC)
codex_auth() {
  python3 -I - "$T/creds/.codex/auth.json" "$1" <<'PY'
import base64, json, sys, time
exp = int(time.time()) + int(sys.argv[2])
pl = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(json.dumps({"exp": exp}).encode()).decode().rstrip("=")
json.dump({"auth_mode": "chatgpt", "tokens": {"access_token": "h.%s.s" % pl, "refresh_token": "R", "account_id": "a"}},
          open(sys.argv[1], "w"))
print(time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime(exp)))
PY
}

head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1081 — remove_colliding builds the overlay half of `reserved` from every hidden-overlay .py basename, and only the fixture half (line 1087) excludes `__init__.py`. If a hidden overlay ships a package marker such as `tests/hidden/__init__.py`, every `__init__.py` the agent adds anywhere (for example a new `src/<pkg>/__init__.py`) is unlinked before the hidden suite and the regression suite run. The solution's imports then break and a correct solution grades as failing, which is the outcome 1.2.11 was meant to prevent. Discard `__init__.py` from the overlay set as well; the code already discards `conftest.py`.
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1087 — The reserved set takes every .py file under a fixture tests/ or test/ directory, so helpers like `helpers.py`, `utils.py` and `_oracle_x.py` are included, not just test modules. The walk at lines 1090-1097 then deletes any agent-added file with one of those basenames anywhere in the tree, including source directories pytest never collects (for example `src/pkg/utils.py`). The basename collision only affects modules pytest collects (`test_*.py` / `*_test.py` under the test paths), so this deletes production code from a correct solution and grades it as failing. The header comment (line 222) and the docstring (line 1076) both say "a fixture test file's basename". Limit the rule to collected test-module names and to files under the test roots.
head/evals/harness/run-ablation.sh:785 — The KF-048 token pre-flight is skipped only for --smoke; it also runs for `--executor host`. In host mode pipeline-run.sh never calls make_home (pipeline-run.sh:648, which is container only). The codex CLI then uses the host's real ~/.codex with its real refresh token and can renew an expired access token. So a host batch is refused (exit 2, REFUSED.txt) for a condition that cannot degrade it. The documentation at lines 110-121 gives the placeholder refresh token as the reason for the check, and that only applies in container mode. Skip or downgrade the check when EXECUTOR is host.
head/evals/harness/run-ablation.sh:503 — Under suite_kind_cap, `(.[$k] // "" | tostring)` turns a present entry of `null` or `false` into "", which falls back to the single cap without an error. Line 192 says a present entry that is not a USD amount is a usage error. In addition, `usd_ok` accepts `0`, so `run_usd_by_type: {build: 0}` is accepted and passes `--max-run-usd 0` to every build trial. Use `has($k)` to detect a present entry and reject a zero cap, matching the `--max-usd` guard at line 365.
head/evals/tests/run-ablation.bats:95 — The comment says "A0 BARE stays 70 min: the suite's phase_defaults declares BARE, so … (80) does not apply". The very next assertion (line 97) expects watchdog_s 9600, which is 80 min, and RAB-27 (line 110) asserts phase_sum_min 80 for a0_bare. One of the two is wrong: either the stale comment should be corrected, or the assertion depends on per-task bounds (DEC-0580) that the comment contradicts. The plan's tmin uses suite phase_defaults BARE: 70 unless the v2 task.yaml declares BARE, so the test is only correct if every v2 task carries `bounds.timeout_min.BARE`. Nothing in this PR checks that.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED
